issues.detail: Rule condition uses prev_in & ~in (falling 1->0), but example vectors 0xFFFFFFFF then 0x00000000 produce out=0xFFFFFFFF, which is consistent; however R3_hold example shows in=1 then in=0 yielding out=1, also consistent. No contradiction found in examples.
Spec says capture when input changes 1->0; rule uses bitwise prev_in & ~in. Alternative semantics: capture only when whole vector transitions from all-ones to all-zeros.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next
issues.alternative: Capture only when entire 32-bit vector goes from 0xFFFFFFFF to 0x00000000

issues.detail: Reset rule example shows reset=1 for two cycles then reset=0 with in=0, expected out=0; consistent with sync reset clearing. No absent verbatim evidence.
R3 example: in=0,1,1,0 with reset=0; expected out=0,0,0,1. Falling edge detected at last row (1->0), out becomes 1 next cycle. Consistent.
